findings.evidence: `grep -rn "transvectionUnit_mul_transvectionUnit_eq_mul_mul" TauCeti` returns only TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Transvection.lean:175 (the declaration); the new proof at SpecialLinearGroup/Transvection.lean:689-693 restates the same equation for `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection`.
findings.fix: Expose the identity once at its natural level as `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection_mul_transvection_eq_mul_mul` beside `commute_transvection`, use it in place of the `hxy` block, and delete the orphaned `TauCeti.transvectionUnit_mul_transvectionUnit_eq_mul_mul`.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.transvectionUnit_mul_transvectionUnit_eq_mul_mul` is the `toGL` image of the determinant-one product identity the PR now proves again as the local `have hxy` in `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.commutatorElement_transvection` (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SpecialLinearGroup/Transvection.lean:689). Its only former consumer, `commutatorElement_transvectionUnit`, was rewired through the SL lemma, so the GL statement is now a derived special case with no use.

findings.evidence: Scheme.lean:341-348 vs Basic.lean:217-223 are the same body with `gaPointsMulEquiv` replaced by `schemePointsMulEquiv`; Scheme.lean:169-173 defines `schemePointsMulEquiv := (groupSchemePointMulEquiv A).symm.trans (gaPointsMulEquiv ..)`, so the transport is available.
findings.fix: Define `gaSchemePointParamMul A p q := groupSchemePointMulEquiv A (gaPointParamMul ((groupSchemePointMulEquiv A).symm p) ((groupSchemePointMulEquiv A).symm q))` and add the compatibility simp lemma `gaSchemePointParamMul A (groupSchemePointMulEquiv A F) (groupSchemePointMulEquiv A G) = groupSchemePointMulEquiv A (gaPointParamMul F G)`; `schemePointsMulEquiv_gaSchemePointParamMul` then follows from `schemePointsMulEquiv_groupSchemePointMulEquiv` and naturality transports for free.
findings.issue: `gaSchemePointParamMul` repeats the `equiv.symm (ofAdd (toAdd _ * toAdd _))` construction of `AdditiveGroup.gaPointParamMul` (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/AdditiveGroup/Basic.lean:217) one level up instead of transporting it along the existing `groupSchemePointMulEquiv`. The result is an independent copy: no lemma relates the two operations, and the naturality `mapValue_gaPointParamMul` (Basic.lean:245) has no scheme-level counterpart, so `commutatorElement_schemePointsMulEquiv_rootSubgroup` cannot be connected to `commutatorElement_rootSubgroupPoints`.

summary: Hypotheses and universes in the new matrix-, algebra-point-, and scheme-point-level statements are minimal and at Mathlib's own level, and moving the type-A relations down to Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (deriving GL via toGL) is the right direction. Two special-case duplications remain: a now-consumerless GL product identity that restates the SL one the PR proves inline, and a scheme-level parameter-product definition that copies rather than transports the algebra-level one.
